g.text: $ aws iam get-account-authorization-details > gaad.json && agentcore-iam-audit --gaad gaad.json # demo account
Agent role can reach other agents' memory
read: GetMemory, RetrieveMemoryRecords, ListEvents, GetEvent, ListMemoryRecords, GetMemoryRecord; write/poison:
CreateEvent, DeleteMemoryRecord on memory not owned by this agent (memory/* or *). Scope Resource to this agent's memory
Agent role can invoke other agents
InvokeAgentRuntime on runtimes not owned by this agent (runtime/* or *). A compromised agent can drive every other
Agent role can use other code interpreters in
InvokeCodeInterpreter, StartCodeInterpreterSession on account code interpreters (code-interpreter/* or *). Code runs
with each interpreter's execution role, not this agent's. Scope to aws.codeinterpreter.v1 or this agent's own.
Privilege escalation via code interpreter (PassRole + Create/InvokeCodeInterpreter)
Can create a code interpreter with an AgentCore role it can pass and run code as that role:
Agent role can read every AgentCore Identity
secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on bedrock-agentcore-identity!default/oauth2/* or /apikey/*: the OAuth client secrets
and API keys of all credential providers in the account's default token vault, not just the ones this agent uses (unless a
resource policy on each secret denies it, which IAM data alone cannot show).
bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com can assume this role with no aws:SourceAccount / aws:SourceArn condition, so
AgentCore resources in other accounts could be configured to use it.
